## arcgis_docs_list_products

**List ArcGIS products and documentation sections**

Lists Esri ArcGIS products that have developer documentation here, or describes one. With no arguments: developer products grouped by category with id, current version line and status. With `product`: its profile (what it is, packages, version lines, documentation sources with page counts, which lookups work, start-here links, known pitfalls, successor if retired). With `product` and `section`: that source's table of contents with refs for arcgis_docs_read. `query` or `category` filter the list; end-user product help (ArcGIS Online, Enterprise, Pro, Survey123, ...) is category "product-help". Does not return page content.

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `product` | string (max 80 chars) | no |  | Product id, name, package or alias, e.g. "js-maps-sdk", "javascript", "@arcgis/core", "arcpy". Omit to list products. |
| `section` | string (max 120 chars) | no |  | With product: a source id from its profile (e.g. "tutorials", "portal", "tools") to get that source's table of contents. |
| `query` | string (max 120 chars) | no |  | Words to filter the product list, e.g. "offline mobile", "webhooks", "3D game engine". |
| `category` | "web" \| "native" \| "game-engine" \| "python" \| "desktop-enterprise" \| "rest-services" \| "ai" \| "specs" \| "devops-oss" \| "support" \| "product-help" \| "all" | no |  | Limit the list to one category. Default: all developer categories (not product-help). |
| `include_legacy` | boolean | no | `false` | Include retired and deprecated products (shown with their successor). |
| `limit` | integer 1..200 | no | `80` |  |
| `cursor` | string (max 600 chars) | no |  | Opaque cursor from a previous call. |

### Examples

```json
{}
```

```json
{"product":"js-maps-sdk"}
```

```json
{"product":"rest-api","section":"portal"}
```

```json
{"query":"offline mobile","include_legacy":true}
```

Markdown text plus `structuredContent` with these fields:

## arcgis_docs_get_versions

**Get ArcGIS product versions and compatibility**

Reports version facts for an ArcGIS product: the current released version and date, the version installed in the current project when it can be detected, pre-release tags, the documentation lines available, install coordinates, Esri's published compatibility pairings (for example JavaScript SDK with ArcGIS Enterprise, Calcite and Arcade), deprecation notices, and refs to the release notes and breaking-changes pages. With `version`, reports on that version. With no arguments, reports every Esri SDK detected in the project. Returns facts and refs, not release-note text.

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `product` | string (max 80 chars) | no |  | Product id, name or package. Omit to report every Esri SDK detected in the current project. |
| `version` | string (max 24 chars) | no |  | A specific version to check, e.g. "4.33", "200.8", "3.6", "11.5", "2.4.3". |

### Examples

```json
{}
```

```json
{"product":"python-api"}
```

```json
{"product":"@arcgis/core","version":"4.33"}
```

### Result

Markdown text plus `structuredContent` with these fields:

- `asOf`: string
- `products`: object[]
  - `id`: string
  - `name`: string
  - `status`: string
  - `documented`: object (optional)
    - `version`: string
    - `released`: string (optional)
    - `source`: string
  - `installable`: object[]
    - `registry`: string
    - `package`: string
    - `version`: string
    - `tag`: string (optional)
    - `published`: string (optional)
    - `source`: string
  - `project`: object (optional)
    - `version`: string
    - `file`: string
    - `behind`: string (optional)
  - `prerelease`: object[]
    - `tag`: string
    - `version`: string
  - `lines`: object[]
    - `id`: string
    - `label`: string
    - `docsUrl`: string
    - `access`: "live" \| "link-only"
    - `symbols`: "live" \| "npm-any-version" \| "none"
  - `install`: string[]
  - `compatibility`: object[]
    - `with`: string
    - `value`: string
    - `unreleased`: boolean
    - `source`: string
  - `lifecycle`: object (optional)
    - `ga`: string (optional)
    - `mature`: string (optional)
    - `retirement`: string (optional)
    - `source`: string
  - `releaseNotes`: object[]
    - `version`: string
    - `ref`: string
  - `notices`: string[]
  - `mismatches`: string[]
- `notes`: string[]

## arcgis_docs_search

**Search ArcGIS developer documentation**

Searches ArcGIS developer documentation and returns ranked hits with title, ref (URL), product, kind, version line, location in the docs and a short excerpt. Covers guides, tutorials, API reference pages and members, REST operations, samples, release notes and product help. Scope with `product` (an id, name, or "product/section" such as "rest-api/portal"); without it the search uses the SDKs detected in the current project or picks the most likely products and says which. `kind` narrows to one content type. Matching is on titles, headings, keywords, descriptions and symbol names, plus the text of pages already read through this server; the status line says whether Esri's full-text site search is also in use. Returns refs for arcgis_docs_read; does not return page bodies. For an exact class, method or endpoint name, arcgis_docs_lookup_symbol is more precise.

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string (max 300 chars) | yes |  | What to find, in plain words or API names, e.g. "cluster points with popups", "applyEdits attachments", "OAuth PKCE". No boolean operators. |
| `product` | string (max 80 chars) | no |  | Product id, name, package, or "product/section". Omit to search the project's SDKs or the most likely products. |
| `kind` | "guide" \| "tutorial" \| "api" \| "sample" \| "release-notes" \| "spec" \| "help" \| "troubleshooting" | no |  | Restrict to one content type. "api" includes REST operations, tools and spec objects. |
| `version` | string (max 24 chars) | no |  | Version line when the product has several, e.g. "v200" for native SDK 200.x, "2.3" for Python. Default: current line. |
| `limit` | integer 1..20 | no | `8` | Number of hits. |
| `cursor` | string (max 600 chars) | no |  | Opaque cursor from a previous call for the next page. |

### Examples

```json
{"query":"cluster points with popups","product":"js-maps-sdk"}
```

```json
{"query":"applyEdits attachments","product":"rest-api/services-enterprise","kind":"api","limit":5}
```

### Result

Markdown text plus `structuredContent` with these fields:

- `query`: string
- `scope`: object
  - `products`: string[]
  - `sources`: string[] (optional)
  - `resolvedFrom`: string (optional)
  - `kind`: string (optional)
  - `line`: string
- `mode`: "local" \| "local+site"
- `total`: integer -9007199254740991..9007199254740991
- `results`: object[]
  - `rank`: integer -9007199254740991..9007199254740991
  - `title`: string
  - `ref`: string
  - `product`: string
  - `source`: string
  - `kind`: "guide" \| "tutorial" \| "api" \| "sample" \| "release-notes" \| "spec" \| "help" \| "troubleshooting" \| "brief"
  - `version`: string (optional)
  - `breadcrumb`: string (optional)
  - `excerpt`: string (optional)
  - `symbolKind`: string (optional)
  - `match`: "symbol" \| "title" \| "heading" \| "keyword" \| "description" \| "body" \| "site"
  - `licenseTier`: string
- `nextCursor`: string (optional)
- `notes`: string[]

## arcgis_docs_read

**Read an ArcGIS documentation page**

Reads one documentation page, API reference page, sample, release-notes page, GitHub file or curated brief and returns clean Markdown with code fences and absolute links. `ref` is a URL from another tool or any URL on Esri's documentation hosts; a "#fragment" selects that section. By default (`view: "auto"`) a document that fits `max_tokens` is returned whole; a larger one returns its opening section plus an outline listing every section id with its size, so the next call can ask for one `section`. `view: "outline"` returns only the outline; `view: "full"` pages through the whole document with `cursor`. On API pages `section` may be a member name; on samples `section: "source"` returns only the code. States the product, version and retrieval date. Does not search: use arcgis_docs_search or arcgis_docs_lookup_symbol to find a ref.

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ref` | string (max 600 chars) | yes |  | Doc URL (or brief:<slug>) returned by another tool, or any URL on an Esri documentation host. May include "#section". |
| `section` | string (max 200 chars) | no |  | One part of the document: a section id or heading text from the outline, a member name on an API page, or "source" on a sample. |
| `view` | "auto" \| "outline" \| "full" | no | `"auto"` | auto: whole doc if it fits, else opening + outline. outline: structure only. full: sequential pages via cursor. |
| `max_tokens` | integer 500..20000 | no | `6000` | Upper bound for this response. |
| `cursor` | string (max 600 chars) | no |  | Opaque cursor from a truncated response to continue it. |

### Examples

```json
{"ref":"https://developers.arcgis.com/javascript/latest/tutorials/add-a-feature-layer/"}
```

```json
{"ref":"https://developers.arcgis.com/javascript/latest/references/core/layers/FeatureLayer/","section":"queryFeatures","max_tokens":3000}
```

```json
{"ref":"brief:ai/overview","view":"outline"}
```

### Result

Markdown text only (no `structuredContent`).

## arcgis_docs_lookup_symbol

**Look up an ArcGIS API symbol**

Looks up one named API entity and returns its declaration and documentation from the product's reference source: classes, interfaces, methods, properties, events and web components (JavaScript, .NET, Kotlin, Swift, Flutter, Qt, Java, Unity, Unreal, Python, ArcPy, Pro SDK), REST operations, Arcade functions, geoprocessing tools and their parameters, and web map / CIM spec objects. `symbol` may be simple or qualified and may include a member ("FeatureLayer.queryFeatures", "arcgis.gis.GIS.content", "arcgis-map.goTo", "arcpy.analysis.Buffer", "applyEdits"). `detail: "signature"` returns the declaration and one line; "summary" (default) adds description, parameters, returns, since/deprecated and one example, or for a type its member index; "full" returns everything within `max_tokens`. If the name is ambiguous the candidates are listed; if it is not found the nearest names are listed. Not for concepts or how-to questions: use arcgis_docs_search.

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `symbol` | string (max 200 chars) | yes |  | Name of a class, member, component, REST operation, function, tool or spec object. Qualified names and "Type.member" are accepted. |
| `product` | string (max 80 chars) | no |  | Product id, name or package. Optional when the symbol is qualified or one Esri SDK is detected in the project. |
| `detail` | "signature" \| "summary" \| "full" | no | `"summary"` | How much to return. |
| `version` | string (max 24 chars) | no |  | Version to read where versioned reference sources exist (any npm version for JavaScript; "v200" for native SDKs). |
| `max_tokens` | integer 300..20000 | no | `3000` | Upper bound for this response. |

### Examples

```json
{"symbol":"FeatureLayer.queryFeatures","product":"js-maps-sdk"}
```

```json
{"symbol":"arcpy.analysis.Buffer","detail":"signature"}
```

### Result

Markdown text only (no `structuredContent`).

## arcgis_docs_find_samples

**Find ArcGIS samples**

Finds runnable ArcGIS samples and templates and returns title, ref, product, platform, language, a one-line summary, the APIs each sample demonstrates when known, and the list of source files. Sources are Esri's sample pages and Esri's Apache-2.0 sample repositories on GitHub (pinned to the release tag where tags are reliable). `uses_api` finds samples that demonstrate a given class or method; `platform` narrows multi-platform SDKs ("maui", "wpf", "winui"); `with_code: true` also returns the main source file of the best hit, within `max_tokens`. Open any hit with arcgis_docs_read (section "source" for code only). Does not return conceptual guides or tutorials: use arcgis_docs_search for those.

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string (max 300 chars) | yes |  | The task the sample should show, e.g. "offline map download", "3D tiles layer", "custom agent with tools". |
| `product` | string (max 80 chars) | no |  | Product id, name or package. Omit to use the SDKs detected in the project. |
| `uses_api` | string (max 120 chars) | no |  | Class, method or component the sample must use, e.g. "OGC3DTilesLayer", "FeatureLayer.applyEdits". |
| `platform` | string (max 40 chars) | no |  | Platform or framework variant when the product has several, e.g. "maui", "wpf", "winui", "react". |
| `with_code` | boolean | no | `false` | Also return the main source file of the top hit. |
| `limit` | integer 1..10 | no | `5` | Number of hits. |
| `max_tokens` | integer 500..20000 | no | `4000` | Upper bound for this response. |

### Examples

```json
{"query":"offline map download","product":"kotlin-maps-sdk"}
```

```json
{"query":"3D tiles layer","uses_api":"OGC3DTilesLayer","with_code":true}
```

### Result

Markdown text plus `structuredContent` with these fields:

- `scope`: object
  - `product`: string
  - `line`: string
  - `platform`: string (optional)
  - `pinnedTo`: string (optional)
- `total`: integer -9007199254740991..9007199254740991
- `results`: object[]
  - `rank`: integer -9007199254740991..9007199254740991
  - `title`: string
  - `ref`: string
  - `product`: string
  - `platform`: string (optional)
  - `language`: string
  - `summary`: string
  - `relevantApis`: string[] (optional)
  - `category`: string (optional)
  - `files`: object[] (optional)
    - `name`: string
    - `ref`: string
    - `bytes`: integer -9007199254740991..9007199254740991 (optional)
  - `origin`: "esri-site" \| "github"
  - `license`: string
  - `apiConfirmed`: boolean (optional)
  - `legacyPattern`: boolean (optional)
- `code`: object (optional)
  - `ref`: string
  - `file`: string
  - `language`: string
  - `text`: string
  - `truncated`: boolean
- `notes`: string[]
